sentences.en: If you collected lists of techniques for doing great work in a lot of different fields, what would the intersection look like?
sentences.cn: 试想，若将各个领域成就卓越的方法收集起来，它们的交集会呈现出怎样的面貌？

sentences.en: I decided to find out by making it.
sentences.cn: 为了寻找答案，我决定尝试梳理一番。

sentences.en: Partly my goal was to create a guide that could be used by someone working in any field.
sentences.cn: 我的初衷是为各行各业的从业者提供一份通用指南。

sentences.en: But I was also curious about the shape of the intersection.
sentences.cn: 但我同样好奇，这些方法的交集究竟为何物？

sentences.en: And one thing this exercise shows is that it does have a definite shape; it's not just a point labelled "work hard."
sentences.cn: 梳理之后，我发现其轮廓十分清晰，绝非“努力工作”这四个字所能概括。

sentences.en: The following recipe assumes you're very ambitious.
sentences.cn: 下文是写给那些有雄心壮志之人看的。

sentences.en: The first step is to decide what to work on.
sentences.cn: 第一步是决定“做什么”。

sentences.en: The work you choose needs to have three qualities: it has to be something you have a natural aptitude for, that you have a deep interest in, and that offers scope to do great work.
sentences.cn: 你选择的工作需同时满足三个条件：天赋：你本就擅长此事；热情：你对它有着极深厚的兴趣；潜力：它拥有成就卓越的广阔空间。

sentences.en: In practice you don't have to worry much about the third criterion.
sentences.cn: 实际上，你大可不必过分纠结第三点。

sentences.en: Ambitious people are if anything already too conservative about it.
sentences.cn: 有雄心的人往往容易低估自己，行事偏于保守。

sentences.en: So all you need to do is find something you have an aptitude for and great interest in. [ 1 ]
sentences.cn: 因此，只需专注于前两点：找到那些既能发挥你天赋，又能让你深深着迷的事。[1]

sentences.en: That sounds straightforward, but it's often quite difficult.
sentences.cn: 这听起来简单，行之维艰。

sentences.en: When you're young you don't know what you're good at or what different kinds of work are like.
sentences.cn: 年轻时，你往往既不了解自己的长处，也不清楚各种工作的真实面貌。

sentences.en: Some kinds of work you end up doing may not even exist yet.
sentences.cn: 有些工作甚至尚未诞生。

sentences.en: So while some people know what they want to do at 14, most have to figure it out.
sentences.cn: 虽有人早在 14 岁便笃定方向，但大多数人仍需在摸索中寻找答案。

sentences.en: The way to figure out what to work on is by working.
sentences.cn: 弄清“做什么”的办法，就是动手去做。若不确定，

sentences.en: If you're not sure what to work on, guess.
sentences.cn: 不妨先猜一个，然后付诸行动。猜错也无妨。

sentences.en: But pick something and get going.
sentences.cn: 涉猎多领域大有裨益，

sentences.en: You'll probably guess wrong some of the time, but that's fine.
sentences.cn: 因为伟大的发现往往诞生于不同领域的碰撞之中。

sentences.en: It's good to know about multiple things; some of the biggest discoveries come from noticing connections between different fields.
sentences.cn: 养成做“个人项目”的习惯。别把“工作”狭隘地理解为他人指派的任务。

sentences.en: Develop a habit of working on your own projects.
sentences.cn: 若哪天你真做出了不起的成就，

sentences.en: Don't let "work" mean something other people tell you to do.
sentences.cn: 它很可能源自你自己的项目。

sentences.en: If you do manage to do great work one day, it will probably be on a project of your own.
sentences.cn: 哪怕它隶属于某个大工程，你也必须是那一小块领地的绝对主宰。

sentences.en: It may be within some bigger project, but you'll be driving your part of it.
sentences.cn: 项目该怎么选？选那些既让你兴奋、又足以承载野心的。

sentences.en: What should your projects be?
sentences.cn: 随着年龄增长，

sentences.en: Whatever seems to you excitingly ambitious.
sentences.cn: 你的品味会进化，

sentences.en: As you grow older and your taste in projects evolves, exciting and important will converge.
sentences.cn: “令人兴奋”和“重要”这两点终将合流。

sentences.en: At 7 it may seem excitingly ambitious to build huge things out of Lego, then at 14 to teach yourself calculus, till at 21 you're starting to explore unanswered questions in physics.
sentences.cn: 7 岁时，用乐高搭建巨型城堡可能就是野心；14 岁时是自学微积分；到了 21 岁，则是探索物理学中的未解之谜。但无论何时，

sentences.en: But always preserve excitingness.
sentences.cn: 请务必呵护那份兴奋感。

sentences.en: There's a kind of excited curiosity that's both the engine and the rudder of great work.
sentences.cn: 有一种令人兴奋的好奇心，它既是成就卓越的引擎，

sentences.en: It will not only drive you, but if you let it have its way, will also show you what to work on.
sentences.cn: 也是舵手。只要追随它，它不仅会驱动你前行，还会指引你的去向。

sentences.en: What are you excessively curious about — curious to a degree that would bore most other people?
sentences.cn: 有什么事是旁人倍感无聊，你却兴致盎然的？

sentences.en: That's what you're looking for.
sentences.cn: 这就是你要找的答案。

sentences.en: Once you've found something you're excessively interested in, the next step is to learn enough about it to get you to one of the frontiers of knowledge.
sentences.cn: 一旦锁定了那个让你极度着迷的领域，下一步就是通过学习，抵达人类知识的疆界。

sentences.en: Knowledge expands fractally, and from a distance its edges look smooth, but once you learn enough to get close to one, they turn out to be full of gaps.
sentences.cn: 知识具有分形（Fractal）结构：远观轮廓平滑，一旦你掌握了足够多的知识并逼近边界，就会发现那里其实布满了缺口。

sentences.en: The next step is to notice them.
sentences.cn: 接下来的任务便是去“看见”这些缺口。

sentences.en: This takes some skill, because your brain wants to ignore such gaps in order to make a simpler model of the world.
sentences.cn: 这需要技巧，因为大脑为了构建简化的世界模型，倾向于忽略它们。

sentences.en: Many discoveries have come from asking questions about things that everyone else took for granted. [ 2 ]
sentences.cn: 许多伟大的发现，正是源于对既定认知的质疑。[2]

sentences.en: If the answers seem strange, so much the better.
sentences.cn: 如果答案看起来很怪异，那再好不过。

sentences.en: Great work often has a tincture of strangeness.
sentences.cn: 伟大的工作往往都带有一丝奇异色彩。

sentences.en: You see this from painting to math.
sentences.cn: 无论是绘画还是数学，都是如此。

sentences.en: It would be affected to try to manufacture it, but if it appears, embrace it.
sentences.cn: 不必刻意猎奇，但若它自然出现，请欣然拥抱。

sentences.en: Boldly chase outlier ideas, even if other people aren't interested in them — in fact, especially if they aren't.
sentences.cn: 大胆追逐那些“离群”的想法，即使——或者说尤其是——其他人都不感兴趣时。

sentences.en: If you're excited about some possibility that everyone else ignores, and you have enough expertise to say precisely what they're all overlooking, that's as good a bet as you'll find. [ 3 ]
sentences.cn: 如果你对某种可能性感到兴奋，而旁人视而不见，且你有足够的专业知识指出他们的疏漏，那么这很可能就是你一直在寻找的最佳良机。[3]

sentences.en: Four steps: choose a field, learn enough to get to the frontier, notice gaps, explore promising ones.
sentences.cn: 选定领域；学至前沿；发现缺口；探索有希望的缺口。

sentences.en: This is how practically everyone who's done great work has done it, from painters to physicists.
sentences.cn: 从画家到物理学家，几乎所有成就卓越者都遵循此道。

sentences.en: Steps two and four will require hard work.
sentences.cn: 第二步和第四步需要艰苦卓绝的努力。

sentences.en: It may not be possible to prove that you have to work hard to do great things, but the empirical evidence is on the scale of the evidence for mortality.
sentences.cn: 虽然未必能从逻辑上证明“卓越必须苦干”，但经验法则就如同生老病死般确凿。

sentences.en: That's why it's essential to work on something you're deeply interested in.
sentences.cn: 正因如此，你必须从事自己深感兴趣的工作。

sentences.en: Interest will drive you to work harder than mere diligence ever could.
sentences.cn: 比起纯粹的勤奋，兴趣才是驱动你全力以赴的更强动力。

sentences.en: The three most powerful motives are curiosity, delight, and the desire to do something impressive.
sentences.cn: 好奇心、愉悦感，以及成就伟业的渴望，是三股最强大的驱动力。

sentences.en: Sometimes they converge, and that combination is the most powerful of all.
sentences.cn: 当这三者交汇，爆发出的能量将无穷无尽。

sentences.en: The big prize is to discover a new fractal bud.
sentences.cn: 终极奖赏在于发现一个新的“分形芽”。

sentences.en: You notice a crack in the surface of knowledge, pry it open, and there's a whole world inside.
sentences.cn: 你在知识的表面窥见一道裂缝，撬开它，里面竟藏着一个全新的世界。

sentences.en: Let's talk a little more about the complicated business of figuring out what to work on.
sentences.cn: 让我们深入审视“决定做什么”这道难题。

sentences.en: The main reason it's hard is that you can't tell what most kinds of work are like except by doing them.
sentences.cn: 其棘手之处在于，除了亲身试错，你很难真正洞悉一份工作的全貌。

sentences.en: Which means the four steps overlap: you may have to work at something for years before you know how much you like it or how good you are at it.
sentences.cn: 这意味着前述的四个步骤往往是交织重叠的：你可能需要投入数年，方能知晓自己是否真心喜爱、或擅长某事。

sentences.en: And in the meantime you're not doing, and thus not learning about, most other kinds of work.
sentences.cn: 而在此时段内，你无暇旁骛，自然也就无从了解其他选项。最坏的情况莫过于，

sentences.en: So in the worst case you choose late based on very incomplete information. [ 4 ]
sentences.cn: 当你终于做出选择时，赖以决策的信息依然残缺不全。[4]

sentences.en: The nature of ambition exacerbates this problem.
sentences.cn: 野心的本质加剧了这一困境。

sentences.en: Ambition comes in two forms, one that precedes interest in the subject and one that grows out of it.
sentences.cn: 野心分两种：一种先于兴趣存在，一种由兴趣滋生。

sentences.en: Most people who do great work have a mix, and the more you have of the former, the harder it will be to decide what to do.
sentences.cn: 大多数成就卓越者兼而有之，但前一种野心越重，决策便越难。

sentences.en: The educational systems in most countries pretend it's easy.
sentences.cn: 各国教育系统大多对这一难题粉饰太平。

sentences.en: They expect you to commit to a field long before you could know what it's really like.
sentences.cn: 它们强迫你在窥见学科全貌之前便选定方向。

sentences.en: And as a result an ambitious person on an optimal trajectory will often read to the system as an instance of breakage.
sentences.cn: 结果导致，一个本在最优路径上行进的有志青年，往往被系统判定为“异类”或“残次品”。

sentences.en: It would be better if they at least admitted it — if they admitted that the system not only can't do much to help you figure out what to work on, but is designed on the assumption that you'll somehow magically guess as a teenager.
sentences.cn: 若教育系统能坦诚相告就好了——承认它不仅爱莫能助，其设计初衷更是建立在“青少年能奇迹般猜对方向”这一假设之上。

sentences.en: They don't tell you, but I will: when it comes to figuring out what to work on, you're on your own.
sentences.cn: 它们不会告诉你，但我会：在决定“做什么”这件事上，你只能孤军奋战。

sentences.en: Some people get lucky and do guess correctly, but the rest will find themselves scrambling diagonally across tracks laid down on the assumption that everyone does.
sentences.cn: 有些人运气好猜对了，而剩下的人，只能在一条预设所有人都已选对的轨道上，逆势横穿，踉跄前行。

sentences.en: What should you do if you're young and ambitious but don't know what to work on?
sentences.cn: 如果你年轻、雄心勃勃却又迷茫无措，该怎么办？

sentences.en: What you should not do is drift along passively, assuming the problem will solve itself.
sentences.cn: 最忌讳的便是随波逐流，妄想问题会自行消解。

sentences.en: You need to take action.
sentences.cn: 你必须行动。

sentences.en: But there is no systematic procedure you can follow.
sentences.cn: 但这并无标准定式。

sentences.en: When you read biographies of people who've done great work, it's remarkable how much luck is involved.
sentences.cn: 读读伟人传记，你会惊讶地发现“运气”占据了多大比重。

sentences.en: They discover what to work on as a result of a chance meeting, or by reading a book they happen to pick up.
sentences.cn: 一次偶遇、一本闲书，都可能成为指路明灯。

sentences.en: So you need to make yourself a big target for luck, and the way to do that is to be curious.
sentences.cn: 因此，你需要让自己成为好运容易命中的“靶子”，而方法就是保持好奇。

sentences.en: Try lots of things, meet lots of people, read lots of books, ask lots of questions. [ 5 ]
sentences.cn: 多尝试，多见人，多读书，多提问。[5]

sentences.en: When in doubt, optimize for interestingness.
sentences.cn: 犹豫不决时，

sentences.en: Fields change as you learn more about them.
sentences.cn: 优先选择“有趣”的那个。

sentences.en: What mathematicians do, for example, is very different from what you do in high school math classes.
sentences.cn: 随着了解深入，领域面貌也会随之改变。数学家真正所做的工作，

sentences.en: So you need to give different types of work a chance to show you what they're like.
sentences.cn: 与高中数学课截然不同。所以，给不同类型的工作一个展露真容的机会。

sentences.en: But a field should become increasingly interesting as you learn more about it.
sentences.cn: 如果你学得越多越觉有趣，那便对了；

sentences.en: If it doesn't, it's probably not for you.
sentences.cn: 反之，它可能并非良配。

sentences.en: Don't worry if you find you're interested in different things than other people.
sentences.cn: 若你的兴趣点异于常人，别担心。

sentences.en: The stranger your tastes in interestingness, the better.
sentences.cn: 品味越怪，越是好事。

sentences.en: Strange tastes are often strong ones, and a strong taste for work means you'll be productive.
sentences.cn: 怪诞的品味通常意味着强烈的热爱，而热爱是高效产出的前提。

sentences.en: And you're more likely to find new things if you're looking where few have looked before.
sentences.cn: 况且，在人迹罕至之地，你更有可能发现新大陆。

sentences.en: One sign that you're suited for some kind of work is when you like even the parts that other people find tedious or frightening.
sentences.cn: 判断你是否适合某项工作的一个试金石是：哪怕是旁人觉得枯燥甚至畏惧的部分，你也乐在其中。

sentences.en: But fields aren't people; you don't owe them any loyalty.
sentences.cn: 但领域不是人，你无需对它们“忠诚”。

sentences.en: If in the course of working on one thing you discover another that's more exciting, don't be afraid to switch.
sentences.cn: 若在研究某事的过程中发现了更令人兴奋的新方向，别害怕，尽管去追。

sentences.en: If you're making something for people, make sure it's something they actually want.
sentences.cn: 如果你的工作是创造事物，请确保那是人们真正想要的。

sentences.en: The best way to do this is to make something you yourself want.
sentences.cn: 最佳捷径便是做你自己想用的东西。

sentences.en: Write the story you want to read; build the tool you want to use.
sentences.cn: 写你想读的故事，造你想用的工具。

sentences.en: Since your friends probably have similar interests, this will also get you your initial audience.
sentences.cn: 既然你的朋友往往与你志趣相投，这也能助你获得最初的用户群。

sentences.en: This should follow from the excitingness rule.
sentences.cn: 这其实契合了“兴奋感法则”。

sentences.en: Obviously the most exciting story to write will be the one you want to read.
sentences.cn: 显而易见，写起来最让你兴奋的故事，正是你自己最想读的那一个。

sentences.en: The reason I mention this case explicitly is that so many people get it wrong.
sentences.cn: 我之所以特意强调此点，是因为太多人本末倒置。

sentences.en: Instead of making what they want, they try to make what some imaginary, more sophisticated audience wants.
sentences.cn: 他们不去做自己想要的，而是试图迎合某个想象中更为“高深”的受众群体。

sentences.en: And once you go down that route, you're lost. [ 6 ]
sentences.cn: 一旦踏上这条歧途，你便离迷失不远了。

sentences.en: There are a lot of forces that will lead you astray when you're trying to figure out what to work on.
sentences.cn: [6]在寻路途中，有太多力量试图引你偏航：自命不凡、盲目跟风、恐惧心理、金钱诱惑、政治因素、

sentences.en: Pretentiousness, fashion, fear, money, politics, other people's wishes, eminent frauds.
sentences.cn: 他人期许，以及那些赫赫有名的欺世盗名之徒。

sentences.en: But if you stick to what you find genuinely interesting, you'll be proof against all of them.
sentences.cn: 但只要坚守你真正感兴趣的事物，这一切都无法撼动你。

sentences.en: If you're interested, you're not astray.
sentences.cn: 只要兴趣尚存，你就未曾迷路。

sentences.en: Following your interests may sound like a rather passive strategy, but in practice it usually means following them past all sorts of obstacles.
sentences.cn: 循兴趣而行，初听似乎是被动的策略，但在实践中，这往往意味着你要追随兴趣，跨越重重阻碍。

sentences.en: You usually have to risk rejection and failure.
sentences.cn: 你常需直面被拒与失败的风险。

sentences.en: So it does take a good deal of boldness.
sentences.cn: 因此，这实则需要极大的 胆识。

sentences.en: But while you need boldness, you don't usually need much planning.
sentences.cn: 胆识虽不可或缺，周详的规划却往往多余。

sentences.en: In most cases the recipe for doing great work is simply: work hard on excitingly ambitious projects, and something good will come of it.
sentences.cn: 多数情况下，成就卓越的秘诀非常简单：在那些既令人兴奋又充满野心的项目上努力工作，好事自会发生。

sentences.en: Instead of making a plan and then executing it, you just try to preserve certain invariants.
sentences.cn: 与其制定缜密的计划并刻板执行，不如坚守几条核心的“不变量”（invariants）。

sentences.en: The trouble with planning is that it only works for achievements you can describe in advance.
sentences.cn: 规划的弊病在于，它仅适用于那些可被预先定义的成就。

sentences.en: You can win a gold medal or get rich by deciding to as a child and then tenaciously pursuing that goal, but you can't discover natural selection that way.
sentences.cn: 若你立志夺得金牌或发家致富，凭坚韧执行确有望达成；但你无法以此发现“自然选择”定律。

sentences.en: I think for most people who want to do great work, the right strategy is not to plan too much.
sentences.cn: 我认为对于大多数渴望成就卓越的人来说，最佳策略是 切勿过度规划。

sentences.en: At each stage do whatever seems most interesting and gives you the best options for the future.
sentences.cn: 在每一阶段，只做当时觉得最有趣、且最能为未来增加选项的事。

sentences.en: I call this approach "staying upwind." This is how most people who've done great work seem to have done it.
sentences.cn: 我称之为“保持上风”（staying upwind）。这似乎是大多数成就卓越者不约而同走出的路径。

sentences.en: Even when you've found something exciting to work on, working on it is not always straightforward.
sentences.cn: 即使找到了令人兴奋的方向，实际执行起来也未必总是一帆风顺。

sentences.en: There will be times when some new idea makes you leap out of bed in the morning and get straight to work.
sentences.cn: 有时，新想法会让你清晨一跃而起，迫不及待地开工；

sentences.en: But there will also be plenty of times when things aren't like that.
sentences.cn: 但也不乏万事滞涩的时刻。

sentences.en: You don't just put out your sail and get blown forward by inspiration.
sentences.cn: 你不能指望升起帆，便坐等灵感之风送你抵达终点。

sentences.en: There are headwinds and currents and hidden shoals.
sentences.cn: 海上有逆风、暗流，亦有暗礁。

sentences.en: So there's a technique to working, just as there is to sailing.
sentences.cn: 工作如航海，是讲究技术的。

sentences.en: For example, while you must work hard, it's possible to work too hard, and if you do that you'll find you get diminishing returns: fatigue will make you stupid, and eventually even damage your health.
sentences.cn: 例如，虽需努力，但也存在“过犹不及”一说。一旦越界，便会出现边际效益递减：疲劳会让你变得迟钝，甚至损害健康。

sentences.en: The point at which work yields diminishing returns depends on the type.
sentences.cn: 边际效益递减的临界点取决于工作类型。

sentences.en: Some of the hardest types you might only be able to do for four or five hours a day.
sentences.cn: 对于那些最耗神的工作，你一天的高效时间或许只有四五个小时。

sentences.en: Ideally those hours will be contiguous.
sentences.cn: 理想情况下，这些时间应是连续的。

sentences.en: To the extent you can, try to arrange your life so you have big blocks of time to work in.
sentences.cn: 生活安排应尽量留出大块的整段时间。若预感到随时会被打断，

sentences.en: You'll shy away from hard tasks if you know you might be interrupted.
sentences.cn: 你就会下意识地规避那些艰难的任务。

sentences.en: It will probably be harder to start working than to keep working.
sentences.cn: “启动”往往比“持续”更难。

sentences.en: You'll often have to trick yourself to get over that initial threshold.
sentences.cn: 你经常需要哄骗自己一下，以跨过最初的门槛。

sentences.en: Don't worry about this; it's the nature of work, not a flaw in your character.
sentences.cn: 别担心，这是工作的固有属性，并非你性格有缺。

sentences.en: Work has a sort of activation energy, both per day and per project.
sentences.cn: 工作存在一种“活化能”（activation energy），无论是按天还是按项目计算皆是如此。

sentences.en: And since this threshold is fake in the sense that it's higher than the energy required to keep going, it's ok to tell yourself a lie of corresponding magnitude to get over it.
sentences.cn: 既然此门槛在某种意义上是虚构的（因为启动所需的能量高于维持运转所需的能量），那么为了跨越它，

sentences.en: It's usually a mistake to lie to yourself if you want to do great work, but this is one of the rare cases where it isn't.
sentences.cn: 撒一个等量的谎亦无不可。若想成就伟大的工作，自欺欺人通常是大忌，但这是一个罕见的例外。

sentences.en: When I'm reluctant to start work in the morning, I often trick myself by saying "I'll just read over what I've got so far." Five minutes later I've found something that seems mistaken or incomplete, and I'm off.
sentences.cn: 若我清晨不愿开工，常骗自己说：“我就把现有的稿子读一遍。” 五分钟后，我不免发现些许错误或遗漏，工作也就自然而然地启动了。

sentences.en: Similar techniques work for starting new projects.
sentences.cn: 类似的技巧也适用于启动新项目。

sentences.en: It's ok to lie to yourself about how much work a project will entail, for example.
sentences.cn: 比如，对所需的工作量撒点谎也无伤大雅。

sentences.en: Lots of great things began with someone saying "How hard could it be?"
sentences.cn: 许多伟大的成就都始于这句名言：“这能有多难？”

sentences.en: This is one case where the young have an advantage.
sentences.cn: 这是年轻人拥有优势的一个特例。

sentences.en: They're more optimistic, and even though one of the sources of their optimism is ignorance, in this case ignorance can sometimes beat knowledge.
sentences.cn: 他们更乐观，虽说这种乐观部分源于无知，但在此刻，无知有时竟能胜过博学。

sentences.en: Try to finish what you start, though, even if it turns out to be more work than you expected.
sentences.cn: 不过，一旦开始，就要尽力完成，哪怕工作量超出了预期。

sentences.en: Finishing things is not just an exercise in tidiness or self-discipline.
sentences.cn: 善始善终不仅关乎整洁与自律。

sentences.en: In many projects a lot of the best work happens in what was meant to be the final stage.
sentences.cn: 在许多项目中，最精彩的发现往往诞生于原以为是收尾的阶段。

sentences.en: Another permissible lie is to exaggerate the importance of what you're working on, at least in your own mind.
sentences.cn: 另一个被允许的谎言是，夸大你手头工作的重要性——至少在你自己心里。

sentences.en: If that helps you discover something new, it may turn out not to have been a lie after all. [ 7 ]
sentences.cn: 如果这能助你发现新事物，那它最终可能就不再是一个谎言了。[7]

sentences.en: Since there are two senses of starting work — per day and per project — there are also two forms of procrastination.
sentences.cn: 既然工作的启动可分为“按日”和“按项目”两类，拖延症便也有两种形式。

sentences.en: Per-project procrastination is far the more dangerous.
sentences.cn: 其中，“项目型拖延”尤为凶险。

sentences.en: You put off starting that ambitious project from year to year because the time isn't quite right.
sentences.cn: 你年复一年地推迟那个宏大的计划，总以此际“时机未到”自我开脱。

sentences.en: When you're procrastinating in units of years, you can get a lot not done. [ 8 ]
sentences.cn: 一旦拖延的单位变成了“年”，你错失的将不可估量。[8]

sentences.en: One reason per-project procrastination is so dangerous is that it usually camouflages itself as work.
sentences.cn: “项目型拖延”之所以致命，因其常披着“工作”的外衣。

sentences.en: You're not just sitting around doing nothing; you're working industriously on something else.
sentences.cn: 你并非游手好闲，甚至可能正兢兢业业地处理着其他琐事。

sentences.en: So per-project procrastination doesn't set off the alarms that per-day procrastination does.
sentences.cn: 因此，它不会像“按日拖延”那样触发警报。你太忙了，

sentences.en: You're too busy to notice it.
sentences.cn: 以至于根本没意识到自己在拖延。

sentences.en: The way to beat it is to stop occasionally and ask yourself: Am I working on what I most want to work on?
sentences.cn: 破解之法是时不时停下来自问：我正在做那件我最想做的事吗？

sentences.en: When you're young it's ok if the answer is sometimes no, but this gets increasingly dangerous as you get older. [ 9 ]
sentences.cn: 年轻时，答“否”尚可原谅；但随着年岁渐长，这个答案将愈发危险。[9]

sentences.en: Great work usually entails spending what would seem to most people an unreasonable amount of time on a problem.
sentences.cn: 伟大的工作，往往意味着在一个问题上投入常人眼中“不合理”的时间。

sentences.en: You can't think of this time as a cost, or it will seem too high.
sentences.cn: 你不能将其视作代价，否则这笔账未免太不划算。

sentences.en: You have to find the work sufficiently engaging as it's happening.
sentences.cn: 你必须在过程中就感受到其迷人之处。

sentences.en: There may be some jobs where you have to work diligently for years at things you hate before you get to the good part, but this is not how great work happens.
sentences.cn: 诚然，有些工作需先忍受多年的枯燥方能苦尽甘来，但这并非成就卓越的通途。

sentences.en: Great work happens by focusing consistently on something you're genuinely interested in.
sentences.cn: 卓越源于持续专注于你真正感兴趣的事物。

sentences.en: When you pause to take stock, you're surprised how far you've come.
sentences.cn: 当你驻足回望，往往会惊讶于自己竟已行进至此。

sentences.en: The reason we're surprised is that we underestimate the cumulative effect of work.
sentences.cn: 我们之所以惊讶，是因为低估了工作的累积之功。

sentences.en: Writing a page a day doesn't sound like much, but if you do it every day you'll write a book a year.
sentences.cn: 日写一页书听起来微不足道，但坚持一年便是一部书稿。关键在于：

sentences.en: That's the key: consistency.
sentences.cn: 持之以恒 （Consistency）。

sentences.en: People who do great things don't get a lot done every day.
sentences.cn: 成大事者并非日日操劳过度，而是日日未曾间断，

sentences.en: They get something done, rather than nothing.
sentences.cn: 而非三天打鱼两天晒网。

sentences.en: If you do work that compounds, you'll get exponential growth.
sentences.cn: 若你从事的是具有复利效应的工作，

sentences.en: Most people who do this do it unconsciously, but it's worth stopping to think about.
sentences.cn: 将收获指数级的爆发。大多数人是在无意识中做到的，

sentences.en: Learning, for example, is an instance of this phenomenon: the more you learn about something, the easier it is to learn more.
sentences.cn: 但这值得我们驻足深思。学习便是此例：知之愈多，学之愈易。

sentences.en: Growing an audience is another: the more fans you have, the more new fans they'll bring you.
sentences.cn: 积累受众亦是如此：粉丝越多，带来的新粉丝便越多。

sentences.en: The trouble with exponential growth is that the curve feels flat in the beginning.
sentences.cn: 指数增长的陷阱在于，曲线初期看似平缓。实则不然，

sentences.en: It isn't; it's still a wonderful exponential curve.
sentences.cn: 它依然是美妙的指数曲线。

sentences.en: But we can't grasp that intuitively, so we underrate exponential growth in its early stages.
sentences.cn: 但我们的直觉无法捕捉微小的起势，因此往往低估了初期的增长。

sentences.en: Something that grows exponentially can become so valuable that it's worth making an extraordinary effort to get it started.
sentences.cn: 具有指数潜力的事物价值连城，值得付出非凡努力去启动。

sentences.en: But since we underrate exponential growth early on, this too is mostly done unconsciously: people push through the initial, unrewarding phase of learning something new because they know from experience that learning new things always takes an initial push, or they grow their audience one fan at a time because they have nothing better to do.
sentences.cn: 但正因初期常被看轻，这通常也是在无意识中完成的：人们熬过学习新知初期那段毫无回报的阶段，是因经验告知这只是暂时；或者他们一个接一个地积累粉丝，仅仅是因为当时无事可做。

sentences.en: If people consciously realized they could invest in exponential growth, many more would do it.
sentences.cn: 若人们能有意识地认知到投资“指数级增长”的价值，定会有更多人投身其中。

sentences.en: Work doesn't just happen when you're trying to.
sentences.cn: 工作并不止于伏案苦干之时。

sentences.en: There's a kind of undirected thinking you do when walking or taking a shower or lying in bed that can be very powerful.
sentences.cn: 当你散步、沐浴或安寝时，发散的思维往往力大无穷。

sentences.en: By letting your mind wander a little, you'll often solve problems you were unable to solve by frontal attack.
sentences.cn: 让思绪片刻游离，常能解开正面强攻无解的难题。但是，若想从中受益，

sentences.en: You have to be working hard in the normal way to benefit from this phenomenon, though.
sentences.cn: 先决条件是常态化的努力工作。你不能光是漫无目的地做白日梦。

sentences.en: You can't just walk around daydreaming.
sentences.cn: 白日梦必须与“刻意工作”交替进行，

sentences.en: The daydreaming has to be interleaved with deliberate work that feeds it questions. [ 10 ]
sentences.cn: 因为后者负责为前者提供素材与问题。[10]

sentences.en: Everyone knows to avoid distractions at work, but it's also important to avoid them in the other half of the cycle.
sentences.cn: 众皆知工作时需心无旁骛，殊不知在循环的另一半（休息/发散）中避免分心同样关键。

sentences.en: When you let your mind wander, it wanders to whatever you care about most at that moment.
sentences.cn: 当思绪游离，它会飘向你此刻最挂怀之事。

sentences.en: So avoid the kind of distraction that pushes your work out of the top spot, or you'll waste this valuable type of thinking on the distraction instead.
sentences.cn: 因此，切勿让琐事将“工作”挤出你大脑关注度的榜首，否则你便将这宝贵的思维模式浪费在鸡毛蒜皮上了。（唯一的例外是：

sentences.en: (Exception: Don't avoid love.)
sentences.cn: 切莫回避爱情。）

sentences.en: Consciously cultivate your taste in the work done in your field.
sentences.cn: 要有意识地培养对本领域工作的品味。

sentences.en: Until you know which is the best and what makes it so, you don't know what you're aiming for.
sentences.cn: 直至知晓何为最佳、因何最佳，方知瞄准何处。

sentences.en: And that is what you're aiming for, because if you don't try to be the best, you won't even be good.
sentences.cn: 这必须是你的目标，因为若不试着成为最佳，你甚至连“好”都做不到。

sentences.en: This observation has been made by so many people in so many different fields that it might be worth thinking about why it's true.
sentences.cn: 这一现象在众多领域被反复验证，值得深思。或许是因为在“野心”这件事上，

sentences.en: It could be because ambition is a phenomenon where almost all the error is in one direction — where almost all the shells that miss the target miss by falling short.
sentences.cn: 几乎所有的误差都是单向的——几乎所有脱靶的子弹皆因射程不够（而非瞄得太高）。

sentences.en: Or it could be because ambition to be the best is a qualitatively different thing from ambition to be good.
sentences.cn: 或许是因为“想成为最好”与“想做得不错”有着质的区别。

sentences.en: Or maybe being good is simply too vague a standard.
sentences.cn: 又或许仅仅是因为“做得不错”这一标准太过模糊。

sentences.en: Probably all three are true. [ 11 ]
sentences.cn: 大概三者皆有之。[11]

sentences.en: Fortunately there's a kind of economy of scale here.
sentences.cn: 所幸，此处存在一种规模经济。

sentences.en: Though it might seem like you'd be taking on a heavy burden by trying to be the best, in practice you often end up net ahead.
sentences.cn: 虽说试图成为最好像是负重前行，但实则净收益往往更高。它令人兴奋，更反而带来一种奇异的自由感。

sentences.en: It's exciting, and also strangely liberating.
sentences.cn: 它让事情变得简单。

sentences.en: It simplifies things.
sentences.cn: 从某种角度看，

sentences.en: In some ways it's easier to try to be the best than to try merely to be good.
sentences.cn: 试图成为最佳，反倒比试图仅仅做得不错要容易得多。

sentences.en: One way to aim high is to try to make something that people will care about in a hundred years.
sentences.cn: 一个拔高目标的方法是：试着做出百年之后人们依然在乎的东西。

sentences.en: Not because their opinions matter more than your contemporaries', but because something that still seems good in a hundred years is more likely to be genuinely good.
sentences.cn: 这并非因为后人的看法比同时代人更重要，而是因为经得起百年考验的东西，更可能是真正的好东西。

sentences.en: Don't try to work in a distinctive style.
sentences.cn: 不要刻意追求独特的风格。

sentences.en: Just try to do the best job you can; you won't be able to help doing it in a distinctive way.
sentences.cn: 你只需全力以赴做到最好，独特的风格自然会随之而来，你想拦都拦不住。

sentences.en: Style is doing things in a distinctive way without trying to.
sentences.cn: 所谓的“风格”，就是你在不经意间做事的独特方式。

sentences.en: Trying to is affectation.
sentences.cn: 刻意为之，那是 矫揉造作 （Affectation）。

sentences.en: Affectation is in effect to pretend that someone other than you is doing the work.
sentences.cn: 矫揉造作，本质上是在假装“不是你”的人在做这份工作。

sentences.en: You adopt an impressive but fake persona, and while you're pleased with the impressiveness, the fakeness is what shows in the work. [ 12 ]
sentences.cn: 你戴上了一副令人印象深刻但虚假的面具。虽然你对那副面具很满意，但最终显露在作品里的，只有那份“虚假”。

sentences.en: The temptation to be someone else is greatest for the young.
sentences.cn: [12]年轻人最容易陷入这种诱惑，想变成别人。

sentences.en: They often feel like nobodies.
sentences.cn: 因为他们觉得自己是个无名小卒。

sentences.en: But you never need to worry about that problem, because it's self-solving if you work on sufficiently ambitious projects.
sentences.cn: 但你完全不必为此焦虑，只要你致力于足够有野心的项目，这个问题便会迎刃而解。

sentences.en: If you succeed at an ambitious project, you're not a nobody; you're the person who did it.
sentences.cn: 一旦你在这样的项目上取得成功，你就不再是无名小卒，

sentences.en: So just do the work and your identity will take care of itself.
sentences.cn: 而是“那个做成了这件事的人”。只管去做，你的身份自然会确立。

sentences.en: "Avoid affectation" is a useful rule so far as it goes, but how would you express this idea positively?
sentences.cn: “避免矫揉造作”是个有用的负面规则，但如果我们要用正面的语言来表达呢？

sentences.en: How would you say what to be, instead of what not to be?
sentences.cn: 如果不说“不要做什么”，而说“要做什么”呢？

sentences.en: The best answer is earnest.
sentences.cn: 最好的答案是：真诚 （Earnest）。

sentences.en: If you're earnest you avoid not just affectation but a whole set of similar vices.
sentences.cn: 如果你足够真诚，你不仅能避免矫揉造作，还能避开一大堆类似的毛病。

sentences.en: The core of being earnest is being intellectually honest.
sentences.cn: 真诚的核心是 智识上的诚实 （Intellectual Honesty）。

sentences.en: We're taught as children to be honest as an unselfish virtue — as a kind of sacrifice.
sentences.cn: 小时候，我们被教育诚实是一种无私的美德，是一种牺牲。

sentences.en: But in fact it's a source of power too.
sentences.cn: 但事实上，诚实也是一种力量的源泉。

sentences.en: To see new ideas, you need an exceptionally sharp eye for the truth.
sentences.cn: 要发现新观点，你需要一双极其锐利、能洞察真相的眼睛。

sentences.en: You're trying to see more truth than others have seen so far.
sentences.cn: 你正试图看到别人未曾看到的真相。

sentences.en: And how can you have a sharp eye for the truth if you're intellectually dishonest?
sentences.cn: 如果你在智识上不诚实，又怎能拥有这双锐眼？

sentences.en: One way to avoid intellectual dishonesty is to maintain a slight positive pressure in the opposite direction.
sentences.cn: 避免智识不诚实的一个方法是，在反方向上保持一点“正压”。

sentences.en: Be aggressively willing to admit that you're mistaken.
sentences.cn: 要极其主动地承认自己的错误。

sentences.en: Once you've admitted you were mistaken about something, you're free.
sentences.cn: 一旦承认了某个错误，你就自由了；

sentences.en: Till then you have to carry it. [ 13 ]
sentences.cn: 否则，你得一直背着它。

sentences.en: Another more subtle component of earnestness is informality.
sentences.cn: [13]真诚的另一个更微妙的成分是 不拘形式 （Informality）。

sentences.en: Informality is much more important than its grammatically negative name implies.
sentences.cn: 它的重要性远超其字面上的“否定”意味所暗示的。

sentences.en: It's not merely the absence of something.
sentences.cn: 它不仅仅是指某种规矩的 缺失，

sentences.en: It means focusing on what matters instead of what doesn't.
sentences.cn: 而是指：专注于重要之事，忽略无关紧要之事。

sentences.en: What formality and affectation have in common is that as well as doing the work, you're trying to seem a certain way as you're doing it.
sentences.cn: 形式主义和矫揉造作的共同点在于：你在做事的同时，还试图在做的过程中表现出某种特定的样子。

sentences.en: But any energy that goes into how you seem comes out of being good.
sentences.cn: 但任何用于“装样子”的能量，都是从“把事做好”的能量中抽走的。

sentences.en: That's one reason nerds have an advantage in doing great work: they expend little effort on seeming anything.
sentences.cn: 这就是为什么极客（Nerds）在成就卓越方面拥有优势：他们很少花心思去装样子。

sentences.en: In fact that's basically the definition of a nerd.
sentences.cn: 事实上，这基本就是“极客”的定义。

sentences.en: Nerds have a kind of innocent boldness that's exactly what you need in doing great work.
sentences.cn: 极客拥有一种天真的莽撞，这正是成就卓越所急需的。这种特质不是学来的，

sentences.en: It's not learned; it's preserved from childhood.
sentences.cn: 而是从童年保留下来的。

sentences.en: So hold onto it.
sentences.cn: 所以，请守住它。

sentences.en: Be the one who puts things out there rather than the one who sits back and offers sophisticated-sounding criticisms of them.
sentences.cn: 做一个把东西做出来并公之于众的人，而不是坐在后面发表高深批评的人。

sentences.en: "It's easy to criticize" is true in the most literal sense, and the route to great work is never easy.
sentences.cn: “批评很容易”这句话在字面意义上也是对的，通往卓越的道路从来都不容易。

sentences.en: There may be some jobs where it's an advantage to be cynical and pessimistic, but if you want to do great work it's an advantage to be optimistic, even though that means you'll risk looking like a fool sometimes.
sentences.cn: 也许在某些工作中，愤世嫉俗和悲观主义是优势，但如果你想成就卓越，乐观才是优势，哪怕这意味着你有时候看起来像个傻瓜。

sentences.en: There's an old tradition of doing the opposite.
sentences.cn: 古老的传统总是教导我们要反其道而行之。

sentences.en: The Old Testament says it's better to keep quiet lest you look like a fool.
sentences.cn: 《旧约》说要保持沉默，以免看起来像个傻瓜。

sentences.en: But that's advice for seeming smart.
sentences.cn: 但那是教你如何 显得 聪明。

sentences.en: If you actually want to discover new things, it's better to take the risk of telling people your ideas.
sentences.cn: 如果你真的想发现新事物，最好还是冒点险，把你的想法告诉别人。

sentences.en: Some people are naturally earnest, and with others it takes a conscious effort.
sentences.cn: 有些人天生真诚，有些人则需要刻意练习。

sentences.en: Either kind of earnestness will suffice.
sentences.cn: 无论哪种都行。但我怀疑，

sentences.en: But I doubt it would be possible to do great work without being earnest.
sentences.cn: 如果不真诚，很难成就卓越。因为这本来就很难。

sentences.en: It's so hard to do even if you are.
sentences.cn: 如果你还要背负矫揉造作、智识不诚实、

sentences.en: You don't have enough margin for error to accommodate the distortions introduced by being affected, intellectually dishonest, orthodox, fashionable, or cool. [ 14 ]
sentences.cn: 墨守成规、追逐时尚或装酷带来的扭曲，你根本没有足够的容错空间。[14]

sentences.en: Great work is consistent not only with who did it, but with itself.
sentences.cn: 卓越的作品不仅与其作者保持一致，其内部也必须协调统一。

sentences.en: It's usually all of a piece.
sentences.cn: 它通常是一个整体。

sentences.en: So if you face a decision in the middle of working on something, ask which choice is more consistent.
sentences.cn: 所以，如果在工作中面临抉择，问问自己：哪个选择能让整体更协调？

sentences.en: You may have to throw things away and redo them.
sentences.cn: 你可能需要把做好的东西扔掉重来。

sentences.en: You won't necessarily have to, but you have to be willing to.
sentences.cn: 不一定非得这么做，但你必须 愿意 这么做。

sentences.en: And that can take some effort; when there's something you need to redo, status quo bias and laziness will combine to keep you in denial about it.
sentences.cn: 这需要勇气；当你需要重做时，现状偏见（Status quo bias）和懒惰会联手让你否认这一需求。为了战胜它们，

sentences.en: To beat this ask: If I'd already made the change, would I want to revert to what I have now?
sentences.cn: 问自己：如果我已经做出了改变，我还愿意改回现在的样子吗？

sentences.en: Have the confidence to cut.
sentences.cn: 要有 做减法 （Cut）的自信。

sentences.en: Don't keep something that doesn't fit just because you're proud of it, or because it cost you a lot of effort.
sentences.cn: 不要仅仅因为你为之感到自豪，或付出了巨大努力，就保留那些不合适的部分。

sentences.en: Indeed, in some kinds of work it's good to strip whatever you're doing to its essence.
sentences.cn: 实际上，在某些工作中，将要做的事情剥离到只剩本质是件好事。

sentences.en: The result will be more concentrated; you'll understand it better; and you won't be able to lie to yourself about whether there's anything real there.
sentences.cn: 结果会更浓缩，你会理解得更透彻，而且你无法再欺骗自己这里面是否有真材实料。

sentences.en: Mathematical elegance may sound like a mere metaphor, drawn from the arts.
sentences.cn: 数学上的优雅 （Mathematical Elegance）听起来像是一个源自艺术的隐喻。

sentences.en: That's what I thought when I first heard the term "elegant" applied to a proof.
sentences.cn: 当我第一次听到用“优雅”来形容数学证明时，我也是这么想的。

sentences.en: But now I suspect it's conceptually prior — that the main ingredient in artistic elegance is mathematical elegance.
sentences.cn: 但我现在怀疑，它在概念上其实是先于艺术的——艺术优雅的主要成分其实就是数学优雅。

sentences.en: At any rate it's a useful standard well beyond math.
sentences.cn: 无论如何，这是一个超越数学领域的有用标准。

sentences.en: Elegance can be a long-term bet, though.
sentences.cn: 不过，追求优雅可能是一项长期赌注。

sentences.en: Laborious solutions will often have more prestige in the short term.
sentences.cn: 从短期看，费力的解决方案往往更具声望。

sentences.en: They cost a lot of effort and they're hard to understand, both of which impress people, at least temporarily.
sentences.cn: 它们耗费巨大心力，且难以理解，这两点都能唬住人——至少暂时能。

sentences.en: Whereas some of the very best work will seem like it took comparatively little effort, because it was in a sense already there.
sentences.cn: 相反，一些最顶尖的工作看起来似乎没费什么劲，因为它在某种意义上 本来就在那里。

sentences.en: It didn't have to be built, just seen.
sentences.cn: 它不需要被建造，只需要被看见。

sentences.en: It's a very good sign when it's hard to say whether you're creating something or discovering it.
sentences.cn: 当你很难分清你是在创造还是在发现时，这是一个非常好的信号。

sentences.en: When you're doing work that could be seen as either creation or discovery, err on the side of discovery.
sentences.cn: 当你做的工作既可被视为创造也可被视为发现时，倾向于将其视为发现。

sentences.en: Try thinking of yourself as a mere conduit through which the ideas take their natural shape.
sentences.cn: 试着把自己想象成一个管道，思想通过你呈现出它们自然的形状。

sentences.en: (Strangely enough, one exception is the problem of choosing a problem to work on.
sentences.cn: （奇怪的是，唯一的例外是“选择做什么”这个问题。

sentences.en: This is usually seen as search, but in the best case it's more like creating something.
sentences.cn: 这通常被视为一种搜索，但在最好的情况下，它更像是一种创造。

sentences.en: In the best case you create the field in the process of exploring it.)
sentences.cn: 在最好的情况下，你在探索的过程中创造了这个领域。）

sentences.en: Similarly, if you're trying to build a powerful tool, make it gratuitously unrestrictive.
sentences.cn: 同样，如果你试图构建一个强大的工具，要让它毫无理由地不设限。

sentences.en: A powerful tool almost by definition will be used in ways you didn't expect, so err on the side of eliminating restrictions, even if you don't know what the benefit will be.
sentences.cn: 一个强大的工具，几乎根据定义，都会被用于你意想不到的方式。所以，哪怕你不知道好处是什么，也要倾向于消除限制。

sentences.en: Great work will often be tool-like in the sense of being something others build on.
sentences.cn: 伟大的工作往往具有工具属性，即它是其他人构建事物的基石。

sentences.en: So it's a good sign if you're creating ideas that others could use, or exposing questions that others could answer.
sentences.cn: 所以，如果你正在创造别人可以使用的想法，或者提出别人可以回答的问题，这是个好兆头。

sentences.en: The best ideas have implications in many different areas.
sentences.cn: 最好的想法在许多不同领域都有其含义。

sentences.en: If you express your ideas in the most general form, they'll be truer than you intended.
sentences.cn: 如果你能以最通用的形式表达你的想法，

sentences.en: True by itself is not enough, of course.
sentences.cn: 它们将比你预期的更加真实。

sentences.en: Great ideas have to be true and new.
sentences.cn: 当然，仅仅真实是不够的。

sentences.en: And it takes a certain amount of ability to see new ideas even once you've learned enough to get to one of the frontiers of knowledge.
sentences.cn: 伟大的想法必须既真实又新颖。即使你学到了知识前沿，想要看到新想法，也需要一定的能力。

sentences.en: In English we give this ability names like originality, creativity, and imagination.
sentences.cn: 在英语中，我们将这种能力称为 原创性 （Originality）、创造力 （Creativity）和 想象力 （Imagination）。

sentences.en: And it seems reasonable to give it a separate name, because it does seem to some extent a separate skill.
sentences.cn: 给它一个单独的名字是合理的，因为它确实在一定程度上是一项独立的技能。

sentences.en: It's possible to have a great deal of ability in other respects — to have a great deal of what's often called technical ability — and yet not have much of this.
sentences.cn: 一个人可能在其他方面能力超群——拥有极高的 技术 能力——但这方面却很匮乏。

sentences.en: I've never liked the term "creative process." It seems misleading.
sentences.cn: 我从来不喜欢“创造过程”这个词。它具有误导性。

sentences.en: Originality isn't a process, but a habit of mind.
sentences.cn: 原创性不是一个过程，而是一种思维习惯。

sentences.en: Original thinkers throw off new ideas about whatever they focus on, like an angle grinder throwing off sparks.
sentences.cn: 原创的思想者无论关注什么，都会迸发出新想法，就像角磨机飞溅出火花一样。

sentences.en: They can't help it.
sentences.cn: 他们忍不住要这么做。

sentences.en: If the thing they're focused on is something they don't understand very well, these new ideas might not be good.
sentences.cn: 如果他们关注的是自己不太了解的事物，这些新想法可能并不怎么样。

sentences.en: One of the most original thinkers I know decided to focus on dating after he got divorced.
sentences.cn: 我认识的一位最具原创性的思想者，在离婚后决定研究约会。

sentences.en: He knew roughly as much about dating as the average 15 year old, and the results were spectacularly colorful.
sentences.cn: 他对约会的了解大概和普通 15 岁少年差不多，结果虽然丰富多彩，却也令人啼笑皆非。

sentences.en: But to see originality separated from expertise like that made its nature all the more clear.
sentences.cn: 但这让我们更清楚地看到：原创性是可以与专业知识分离的。

sentences.en: I don't know if it's possible to cultivate originality, but there are definitely ways to make the most of however much you have.
sentences.cn: 我不知道原创性是否可以培养，但肯定有办法让你现有的原创性发挥最大价值。

sentences.en: For example, you're much more likely to have original ideas when you're working on something.
sentences.cn: 例如，当你在做具体工作时，比空想更容易产生原创想法。

sentences.en: Original ideas don't come from trying to have original ideas.
sentences.cn: 原创想法不是通过“试图有原创想法”得来的，

sentences.en: They come from trying to build or understand something slightly too difficult. [ 15 ]
sentences.cn: 而是通过“试图建立或理解某个稍微有点难度的东西”得来的。[15]

sentences.en: Talking or writing about the things you're interested in is a good way to generate new ideas.
sentences.cn: 谈论或写作 你感兴趣的事情，是产生新想法的好方法。

sentences.en: When you try to put ideas into words, a missing idea creates a sort of vacuum that draws it out of you.
sentences.cn: 当你试图将思想转化为语言时，缺失的想法会形成某种真空，把它从你的脑海中吸出来。

sentences.en: Indeed, there's a kind of thinking that can only be done by writing.
sentences.cn: 事实上，有一种思考只能通过写作来完成。

sentences.en: Changing your context can help.
sentences.cn: 改变环境 也有帮助。

sentences.en: If you visit a new place, you'll often find you have new ideas there.
sentences.cn: 到一个新地方，你常会发现新想法。

sentences.en: The journey itself often dislodges them.
sentences.cn: 旅途本身往往能把它们震出来。

sentences.en: But you may not have to go far to get this benefit.
sentences.cn: 你不必跑很远，有时散个步就够了。

sentences.en: Sometimes it's enough just to go for a walk. [ 16 ]
sentences.cn: [16]在 话题空间 （Topic space）里旅行也有用。

sentences.en: It also helps to travel in topic space.
sentences.cn: 如果你探索许多不同的话题，

sentences.en: You'll have more new ideas if you explore lots of different topics, partly because it gives the angle grinder more surface area to work on, and partly because analogies are an especially fruitful source of new ideas.
sentences.cn: 你会拥有更多新想法。部分原因是这给了“角磨机”更大的接触面积，部分原因是 类比 （Analogies）是新想法极其丰沃的来源。

sentences.en: Don't divide your attention evenly between many topics though, or you'll spread yourself too thin.
sentences.cn: 不过，不要把注意力 平均 分配给许多话题，那样你会过于分散。

sentences.en: You want to distribute it according to something more like a power law.
sentences.cn: 你应该按照类似 幂律 （Power law）的方式分配：对少数几个话题保持专业性的好奇，

sentences.en: [ 17 ] Be professionally curious about a few topics and idly curious about many more.
sentences.cn: 对许多其他话题保持闲散的好奇。[17]

sentences.en: Curiosity and originality are closely related.
sentences.cn: 好奇心与原创性密切相关。

sentences.en: Curiosity feeds originality by giving it new things to work on.
sentences.cn: 好奇心通过提供新素材来滋养原创性。

sentences.en: But the relationship is closer than that.
sentences.cn: 但它们的关系比这更紧密。

sentences.en: Curiosity is itself a kind of originality; it's roughly to questions what originality is to answers.
sentences.cn: 好奇心本身就是一种原创性；它对于问题的作用，就像原创性对于答案的作用。

sentences.en: And since questions at their best are a big component of answers, curiosity at its best is a creative force.
sentences.cn: 既然最好的问题本身就是答案的重要组成部分，那么最好的好奇心本质上就是一种创造力。

sentences.en: Having new ideas is a strange game, because it usually consists of seeing things that were right under your nose.
sentences.cn: 获得新想法是一个奇怪的游戏，因为它通常意味着 看到那些就在你鼻子底下的东西。

sentences.en: Once you've seen a new idea, it tends to seem obvious.
sentences.cn: 一旦看到了新想法，它往往显得显而易见。

sentences.en: Why did no one think of this before?
sentences.cn: 为什么以前没人想到呢？

sentences.en: When an idea seems simultaneously novel and obvious, it's probably a good one.
sentences.cn: 当一个想法看起来既新颖又显而易见时，

sentences.en: Seeing something obvious sounds easy.
sentences.cn: 它很可能是一个好想法。

sentences.en: And yet empirically having new ideas is hard.
sentences.cn: 看到显而易见的东西听起来很容易。

sentences.en: What's the source of this apparent contradiction?
sentences.cn: 但经验告诉我们，获得新想法很难。

sentences.en: It's that seeing the new idea usually requires you to change the way you look at the world.
sentences.cn: 这种矛盾的根源是什么？原因在于，看到新想法通常需要你 改变看世界的方式。

sentences.en: We see the world through models that both help and constrain us.
sentences.cn: 我们通过模型来看世界，这些模型既帮助了我们，也限制了我们。

sentences.en: When you fix a broken model, new ideas become obvious.
sentences.cn: 当你修复了一个破碎的模型，新想法就会变得显而易见。

sentences.en: But noticing and fixing a broken model is hard.
sentences.cn: 但 发现并修复破碎的模型是很难的。

sentences.en: That's how new ideas can be both obvious and yet hard to discover: they're easy to see after you do something hard.
sentences.cn: 这就是为什么新想法既显而易见又难以发现：在你做了一件困难的事情（修复模型）之后，它们才变得容易看见。

sentences.en: One way to discover broken models is to be stricter than other people.
sentences.cn: 发现破碎模型的一个方法是 比别人更严谨 （Stricter）。

sentences.en: Broken models of the world leave a trail of clues where they bash against reality.
sentences.cn: 破碎的世界模型在与现实碰撞时会留下一串线索。

sentences.en: Most people don't want to see these clues.
sentences.cn: 大多数人不想看到这些线索。

sentences.en: It would be an understatement to say that they're attached to their current model; it's what they think in; so they'll tend to ignore the trail of clues left by its breakage, however conspicuous it may seem in retrospect.
sentences.cn: 说他们依恋现有模型都算是轻描淡写了；那是他们思考的依凭；所以他们倾向于忽略模型破裂留下的线索，无论事后看来这些线索有多么显眼。

sentences.en: To find new ideas you have to seize on signs of breakage instead of looking away.
sentences.cn: 要发现新想法，你必须 抓住这些破裂的迹象，而不是把视线移开。

sentences.en: That's what Einstein did.
sentences.cn: 这就是爱因斯坦所做的。

sentences.en: He was able to see the wild implications of Maxwell's equations not so much because he was looking for new ideas as because he was stricter.
sentences.cn: 他能看到麦克斯韦方程组的疯狂含义，与其说是因为他在寻找新想法，不如说是因为他更严谨。

sentences.en: The other thing you need is a willingness to break rules.
sentences.cn: 你需要具备的另一种特质是 打破规则的意愿。

sentences.en: Paradoxical as it sounds, if you want to fix your model of the world, it helps to be the sort of person who's comfortable breaking rules.
sentences.cn: 这听起来很矛盾，但如果你想修复世界模型，最好做一个乐于打破规则的人。

sentences.en: From the point of view of the old model, which everyone including you initially shares, the new model usually breaks at least implicit rules.
sentences.cn: 从旧模型的角度看（这也是包括你在内的所有人最初持有的观点），新模型通常打破了至少某些隐形规则。

sentences.en: Few understand the degree of rule-breaking required, because new ideas seem much more conservative once they succeed.
sentences.cn: 很少有人理解这种“破坏”需要达到什么程度，因为新想法一旦成功，

sentences.en: They seem perfectly reasonable once you're using the new model of the world they brought with them.
sentences.cn: 看起来就保守多了。一旦你使用了新模型，它们看起来就完全合理。

sentences.en: But they didn't at the time; it took the greater part of a century for the heliocentric model to be generally accepted, even among astronomers, because it felt so wrong.
sentences.cn: 但在当时并非如此；日心说花了将近一个世纪才被普遍接受，甚至在天文学家中间也是如此，因为它当时感觉太“错”了。

sentences.en: Indeed, if you think about it, a good new idea has to seem bad to most people, or someone would have already explored it.
sentences.cn: 事实上，如果你仔细想想，一个好的新想法必须在大多数人看来是“坏”的，否则早就有人去探索了。

sentences.en: So what you're looking for is ideas that seem crazy, but the right kind of crazy.
sentences.cn: 所以你要寻找的是那些 看起来疯狂，但疯狂得恰到好处的想法。

sentences.en: How do you recognize these?
sentences.cn: 怎么辨别呢？

sentences.en: You can't with certainty.
sentences.cn: 你无法确切知道。

sentences.en: Often ideas that seem bad are bad.
sentences.cn: 通常看起来坏的想法就是坏的。

sentences.en: But ideas that are the right kind of crazy tend to be exciting; they're rich in implications; whereas ideas that are merely bad tend to be depressing.
sentences.cn: 但是，“好”的疯狂想法往往令人兴奋，充满潜在含义；而仅仅是“坏”的想法往往令人沮丧。

sentences.en: There are two ways to be comfortable breaking rules: to enjoy breaking them, and to be indifferent to them.
sentences.cn: 有两种方式可以让你从容地打破规则：一种是 享受 打破规则，一种是 漠视 规则。

sentences.en: I call these two cases being aggressively and passively independent-minded.
sentences.cn: 我称之为“攻击性” （Aggressively）和 “被动性”（Passively）的独立思考。

sentences.en: The aggressively independent-minded are the naughty ones.
sentences.cn: 攻击性的独立思考者 是淘气包。

sentences.en: Rules don't merely fail to stop them; breaking rules gives them additional energy.
sentences.cn: 规则不仅无法阻止他们，打破规则反而给了他们额外的能量。

sentences.en: For this sort of person, delight at the sheer audacity of a project sometimes supplies enough activation energy to get it started.
sentences.cn: 对于这类人，仅仅是对项目“胆大包天”的喜悦，有时就足以提供启动所需的活化能。

sentences.en: The other way to break rules is not to care about them, or perhaps even to know they exist.
sentences.cn: 另一种打破规则的方式是不在乎它们，甚至不知道它们的存在。

sentences.en: This is why novices and outsiders often make new discoveries; their ignorance of a field's assumptions acts as a source of temporary passive independent-mindedness.
sentences.cn: 这就是为什么 新手和局外人 经常会有新发现；他们对领域内既定假设的无知，成为了一种暂时的、被动的独立思考源泉。

sentences.en: Aspies also seem to have a kind of immunity to conventional beliefs.
sentences.cn: 阿斯伯格综合征（Aspies）患者似乎也对传统观念有一种免疫力。

sentences.en: Several I know say that this helps them to have new ideas.
sentences.cn: 我认识好几个这样的人，他们说这对产生新想法很有帮助。

sentences.en: Strictness plus rule-breaking sounds like a strange combination.
sentences.cn: 严谨 + 打破规则，这听起来像是一个奇怪的组合。

sentences.en: In popular culture they're opposed.
sentences.cn: 在流行文化中，这两者是对立的。

sentences.en: But popular culture has a broken model in this respect.
sentences.cn: 但这正是流行文化的模型破碎之处。

sentences.en: It implicitly assumes that issues are trivial ones, and in trivial matters strictness and rule-breaking are opposed.
sentences.cn: 它隐含地假设问题都是琐碎的；在琐碎的事情上，严谨和打破规则确实是对立的。

sentences.en: But in questions that really matter, only rule-breakers can be truly strict.
sentences.cn: 但在真正重要的问题上，只有打破规则者才能做到真正的严谨。

sentences.en: An overlooked idea often doesn't lose till the semifinals.
sentences.cn: 一个被忽视的好点子，往往能撑过初赛，

sentences.en: You do see it, subconsciously, but then another part of your subconscious shoots it down because it would be too weird, too risky, too much work, too controversial.
sentences.cn: 却输在半决赛。你的潜意识其实看到了它，但随即把它枪毙了——因为它太怪异、太冒险、太费劲，或者太具争议性。

sentences.en: This suggests an exciting possibility: if you could turn off such filters, you could see more new ideas.
sentences.cn: 这暗示了一个令人兴奋的可能性：如果你能关掉这些潜意识过滤器，你就能看到更多新想法。

sentences.en: One way to do that is to ask what would be good ideas for someone else to explore.
sentences.cn: 一个欺骗潜意识的方法是问自己：如果是别人来做，什么是一个好点子？

sentences.en: Then your subconscious won't shoot them down to protect you.
sentences.cn: 这样你的潜意识就不会为了保护你而枪毙它。

sentences.en: You could also discover overlooked ideas by working in the other direction: by starting from what's obscuring them.
sentences.cn: 你也可以反其道而行之：从那些“遮蔽物”入手。每一个被奉为圭臬但实际上错误的原则周围，

sentences.en: Every cherished but mistaken principle is surrounded by a dead zone of valuable ideas that are unexplored because they contradict it.
sentences.cn: 都环绕着一片“死角”——那里充满了因与原则相悖而未被探索的宝贵想法。

sentences.en: Religions are collections of cherished but mistaken principles.
sentences.cn: 宗教 就是这类原则的集合。

sentences.en: So anything that can be described either literally or metaphorically as a religion will have valuable unexplored ideas in its shadow.
sentences.cn: 任何可以被字面上或隐喻上称为“宗教”的东西，在其阴影下都藏着未被挖掘的宝藏。

sentences.en: Copernicus and Darwin both made discoveries of this type. [ 18 ]
sentences.cn: 哥白尼和达尔文都做出了这类发现。[18]

sentences.en: What are people in your field religious about, in the sense of being too attached to some principle that might not be as self-evident as they think?
sentences.cn: 在你所处的领域，人们对什么东西持有“宗教般”的执念？有什么原则是他们深信不疑，但其实并非不证自明的？

sentences.en: What becomes possible if you discard it?
sentences.cn: 如果你抛弃它，会有什么新的可能？

sentences.en: People show much more originality in solving problems than in deciding which problems to solve.
sentences.cn: 人们在 解决问题 时表现出的原创性，远超在 决定解决什么问题 时。

sentences.en: Even the smartest can be surprisingly conservative when deciding what to work on.
sentences.cn: 即使是最聪明的人，在选题时也保守得惊人。

sentences.en: People who'd never dream of being fashionable in any other way get sucked into working on fashionable problems.
sentences.cn: 那些在其他方面绝不随大流的人，却常常被吸进“时髦问题”的黑洞。

sentences.en: One reason people are more conservative when choosing problems than solutions is that problems are bigger bets.
sentences.cn: 人们在选题上保守，部分是因为 问题是更大的赌注。

sentences.en: A problem could occupy you for years, while exploring a solution might only take days.
sentences.cn: 一个问题可能占据你数年光阴，而探索一个解决方案可能只需几天。

sentences.en: But even so I think most people are too conservative.
sentences.cn: 但即便如此，大多数人还是太保守了。

sentences.en: They're not merely responding to risk, but to fashion as well.
sentences.cn: 他们不仅是在规避风险，更是在追逐时尚。

sentences.en: Unfashionable problems are undervalued.
sentences.cn: 不时髦的问题被严重低估了。

sentences.en: One of the most interesting kinds of unfashionable problem is the problem that people think has been fully explored, but hasn't.
sentences.cn: 最有趣的一种不时髦问题是：那些人们以为已经被研究透了，其实并没有的问题。

sentences.en: Great work often takes something that already exists and shows its latent potential.
sentences.cn: 伟大的工作往往是发掘既有事物的潜在价值。

sentences.en: Durer and Watt both did this.
sentences.cn: 丢勒（Durer）和瓦特（Watt）都是如此。

sentences.en: So if you're interested in a field that others think is tapped out, don't let their skepticism deter you.
sentences.cn: 如果你对某个别人认为已经“枯竭”的领域感兴趣，别让他们的怀疑劝退你。

sentences.en: People are often wrong about this.
sentences.cn: 在这件事上，大家通常是错的。

sentences.en: Working on an unfashionable problem can be very pleasing.
sentences.cn: 研究不时髦的问题是一种愉悦的体验。

sentences.en: There's no hype or hurry.
sentences.cn: 没有炒作，没有匆忙。

sentences.en: Opportunists and critics are both occupied elsewhere.
sentences.cn: 投机者和批评家都忙着去别处凑热闹。

sentences.en: The existing work often has an old-school solidity.
sentences.cn: 现有的工作往往带有一种老派的坚实感。

sentences.en: And there's a satisfying sense of economy in cultivating ideas that would otherwise be wasted.
sentences.cn: 而且，利用那些本会被浪费的想法，会给你一种令人满足的“经济感”。

sentences.en: But the most common type of overlooked problem is not explicitly unfashionable in the sense of being out of fashion.
sentences.cn: 但最常见的“被忽视问题”，并非显而易见地“不时髦”，

sentences.en: It just doesn't seem to matter as much as it actually does.
sentences.cn: 它只是 看起来没那么重要。

sentences.en: How do you find these?
sentences.cn: 如何找到它们？

sentences.en: By being self-indulgent — by letting your curiosity have its way, and tuning out, at least temporarily, the little voice in your head that says you should only be working on "important" problems.
sentences.cn: 做一个自我放纵的人 ——让你的好奇心做主，暂时屏蔽脑子里那个告诉你只做“重要”工作的声音。

sentences.en: You do need to work on important problems, but almost everyone is too conservative about what counts as one.
sentences.cn: 你确实需要解决重要问题，但几乎所有人对“重要”的定义都太保守了。

sentences.en: And if there's an important but overlooked problem in your neighborhood, it's probably already on your subconscious radar screen.
sentences.cn: 如果你身边有一个重要但被忽视的问题，它很可能已经出现在你潜意识的雷达上了。

sentences.en: So try asking yourself: if you were going to take a break from "serious" work to work on something just because it would be really interesting, what would you do?
sentences.cn: 试着问自己：如果你要从“正经”工作中抽身，纯粹为了好玩去做点什么，你会做什么？

sentences.en: The answer is probably more important than it seems.
sentences.cn: 答案可能比看起来重要得多。

sentences.en: Originality in choosing problems seems to matter even more than originality in solving them.
sentences.cn: 选题的原创性比解题的原创性更重要。

sentences.en: That's what distinguishes the people who discover whole new fields.
sentences.cn: 这正是开创全新领域之人的独特之处。

sentences.en: So what might seem to be merely the initial step — deciding what to work on — is in a sense the key to the whole game.
sentences.cn: 因此，决定“做什么”这看似只是初始的一步，在某种意义上却是整场游戏的关键。

sentences.en: Few grasp this.
sentences.cn: 很少有人理解这一点。

sentences.en: One of the biggest misconceptions about new ideas is about the ratio of question to answer in their composition.
sentences.cn: 关于新想法最大的误解之一，就是关于“问题”和“答案”的比例。

sentences.en: People think big ideas are answers, but often the real insight was in the question.
sentences.cn: 人们以为大想法是答案，但通常，真正的洞见在于问题。

sentences.en: Part of the reason we underrate questions is the way they're used in schools.
sentences.cn: 我们低估问题，部分归咎于学校的教育方式。

sentences.en: In schools they tend to exist only briefly before being answered, like unstable particles.
sentences.cn: 在学校里，问题就像不稳定的粒子，刚出现就被答案消灭了。

sentences.en: But a really good question can be much more than that.
sentences.cn: 但一个真正的好问题远不止于此。

sentences.en: A really good question is a partial discovery.
sentences.cn: 一个好问题，本身就是部分的发现。

sentences.en: How do new species arise?
sentences.cn: “新物种是如何产生的？

sentences.en: Is the force that makes objects fall to earth the same as the one that keeps planets in their orbits?
sentences.cn: ”“让苹果落地的力与维系行星运转的力是同一种力吗？” 仅仅是提出这些问题，

sentences.en: By even asking such questions you were already in excitingly novel territory.
sentences.cn: 你就已经踏入了激动人心的新领域。

sentences.en: Unanswered questions can be uncomfortable things to carry around with you.
sentences.cn: 随身携带未解之谜可能会让人不舒服。

sentences.en: But the more you're carrying, the greater the chance of noticing a solution — or perhaps even more excitingly, noticing that two unanswered questions are the same.
sentences.cn: 但你带着的谜题越多，发现答案的机会就越大——甚至更令人兴奋的是，你会发现两个未解之谜原来是同一个问题。

sentences.en: Sometimes you carry a question for a long time.
sentences.cn: 有些问题你可能要背负很久。

sentences.en: Great work often comes from returning to a question you first noticed years before — in your childhood, even — and couldn't stop thinking about.
sentences.cn: 伟大的工作往往源于回归你多年前——甚至童年时——注意到的那个问题。

sentences.en: People talk a lot about the importance of keeping your youthful dreams alive, but it's just as important to keep your youthful questions alive. [ 19 ]
sentences.cn: 人们常说要守护年轻时的梦想，但守护年轻时的问题同样重要。[19]

sentences.en: This is one of the places where actual expertise differs most from the popular picture of it.
sentences.cn: 这是真正的专家与大众印象最不同的地方。

sentences.en: In the popular picture, experts are certain.
sentences.cn: 大众眼里的专家是确定的。

sentences.en: But actually the more puzzled you are, the better, so long as (a) the things you're puzzled about matter, and (b) no one else understands them either.
sentences.cn: 但实际上，你越困惑越好，只要：(a) 让你困惑的事很重要，且 (b) 没人懂它。

sentences.en: Think about what's happening at the moment just before a new idea is discovered.
sentences.cn: 想一想新想法诞生前的那一刻。

sentences.en: Often someone with sufficient expertise is puzzled about something.
sentences.cn: 通常是一个拥有足够专业知识的人对某事感到困惑。

sentences.en: Which means that originality consists partly of puzzlement — of confusion!
sentences.cn: 这意味着，原创性部分构筑于困惑之上！

sentences.en: You have to be comfortable enough with the world being full of puzzles that you're willing to see them, but not so comfortable that you don't want to solve them. [ 20 ]
sentences.cn: 你必须能够接受世界充满谜团，并愿意看见它们，但又不能接受它们一直无解。[20]

sentences.en: It's a great thing to be rich in unanswered questions.
sentences.cn: “富拥”未解之谜是件好事。

sentences.en: And this is one of those situations where the rich get richer, because the best way to acquire new questions is to try answering existing ones.
sentences.cn: 这是“富者越富”的场景之一，因为获取新问题的最好方法就是尝试回答旧问题。

sentences.en: Questions don't just lead to answers, but also to more questions.
sentences.cn: 问题不仅通向答案，更通向更多的问题。

sentences.en: The best questions grow in the answering.
sentences.cn: 最好的问题是在回答的过程中长大的。

sentences.en: You notice a thread protruding from the current paradigm and try pulling on it, and it just gets longer and longer.
sentences.cn: 你注意到现有范式中露出了一个小线头，试着拉了一下，结果它越拉越长。

sentences.en: So don't require a question to be obviously big before you try answering it.
sentences.cn: 所以，别指望在动手前就确定一个问题是否足够“大”。

sentences.en: You can rarely predict that.
sentences.cn: 你很难预测。

sentences.en: It's hard enough even to notice the thread, let alone to predict how much will unravel if you pull on it.
sentences.cn: 能注意到线头已属不易，更别提预测拉出来会有多长了。

sentences.en: It's better to be promiscuously curious — to pull a little bit on a lot of threads, and see what happens.
sentences.cn: 最好保持一种“滥情”的好奇心（Promiscuously curious）——随处拉拉线头，看看会发生什么。

sentences.en: Big things start small.
sentences.cn: 大事往往起于微末。

sentences.en: The initial versions of big things were often just experiments, or side projects, or talks, which then grew into something bigger.
sentences.cn: 许多宏大项目的初版只是一个实验、一个副业，或一次谈话。

sentences.en: So start lots of small things.
sentences.cn: 所以，多开几个小头。

sentences.en: Being prolific is underrated.
sentences.cn: 多产（Prolific）被低估了。

sentences.en: The more different things you try, the greater the chance of discovering something new.
sentences.cn: 你尝试的东西越多，发现新事物的概率就越大。

sentences.en: Understand, though, that trying lots of things will mean trying lots of things that don't work.
sentences.cn: 但要明白，尝试多意味着失败多。

sentences.en: You can't have a lot of good ideas without also having a lot of bad ones. [ 21 ]
sentences.cn: 你不可能只拥有很多好主意，而不伴随着很多坏主意。

sentences.en: Though it sounds more responsible to begin by studying everything that's been done before, you'll learn faster and have more fun by trying stuff.
sentences.cn: [21]虽然“先把前人的研究都看完再动手”听起来更负责任，但 通过动手尝试，你学得更快，也更有趣。

sentences.en: And you'll understand previous work better when you do look at it.
sentences.cn: 而且等你回过头看前人的工作时，你会理解得更透彻。

sentences.en: So err on the side of starting.
sentences.cn: 所以，宁可贸然开始。

sentences.en: Which is easier when starting means starting small; those two ideas fit together like two puzzle pieces.
sentences.cn: 当“开始”意味着“从小做起”时，这就更容易了；这两个理念就像两块拼图一样契合。

sentences.en: How do you get from starting small to doing something great?
sentences.cn: 如何从小事变成大事？

sentences.en: By making successive versions.
sentences.cn: 通过版本的迭代。

sentences.en: Great things are almost always made in successive versions.
sentences.cn: 伟大的事物几乎都是迭代出来的。

sentences.en: You start with something small and evolve it, and the final version is both cleverer and more ambitious than anything you could have planned.
sentences.cn: 你从一个小东西开始，不断进化，最终版本将比你计划的任何东西都更聪明、更宏大。

sentences.en: It's particularly useful to make successive versions when you're making something for people — to get an initial version in front of them quickly, and then evolve it based on their response.
sentences.cn: 当你为用户创造产品时，迭代尤为重要——尽快把初版推到他们面前，根据反馈进化。先尝试最简单、最可能行得通的方法。

sentences.en: Begin by trying the simplest thing that could possibly work.
sentences.cn: 令人惊讶的是，它往往真的行得通。

sentences.en: Surprisingly often, it does.
sentences.cn: 即使不行，

sentences.en: If it doesn't, this will at least get you started.
sentences.cn: 至少你已经上路了。

sentences.en: Don't try to cram too much new stuff into any one version.
sentences.cn: 别试图在一个版本里塞进太多新东西。

sentences.en: There are names for doing this with the first version (taking too long to ship) and the second (the second system effect), but these are both merely instances of a more general principle.
sentences.cn: 这在第一版叫“发版太慢”，在第二版叫“第二系统效应”（Second-system effect），但这都是同一个原则的体现。

sentences.en: An early version of a new project will sometimes be dismissed as a toy.
sentences.cn: 新项目的早期版本有时会被贬低为“玩具”。

sentences.en: It's a good sign when people do this.
sentences.cn: 如果有人这么说，那是好兆头。

sentences.en: That means it has everything a new idea needs except scale, and that tends to follow. [ 22 ]
sentences.cn: 这意味着它具备了新想法所需的一切，除了规模，而规模往往随之而来。[22]

sentences.en: The alternative to starting with something small and evolving it is to plan in advance what you're going to do.
sentences.cn: “从小做起、持续进化”的对立面是“预先规划”。

sentences.en: And planning does usually seem the more responsible choice.
sentences.cn: 规划通常看起来更负责任。

sentences.en: It sounds more organized to say "we're going to do x and then y and then z" than "we're going to try x and see what happens." And it is more organized ; it just doesn't work as well.
sentences.cn: 说“我们要先做x，再做y，最后做z”听起来比“我们要试下x，看看会发生什么”更有条理。它确实更有条理，只是效果没那么好。

sentences.en: Planning per se isn't good.
sentences.cn: 规划本身不是好事。

sentences.en: It's sometimes necessary, but it's a necessary evil — a response to unforgiving conditions.
sentences.cn: 它有时是必要的，但是一种“必要的恶”——是对无情条件的妥协。

sentences.en: It's something you have to do because you're working with inflexible media, or because you need to coordinate the efforts of a lot of people.
sentences.cn: 是因为你使用的媒介不灵活，或者你需要协调大量人员，才不得不规划。

sentences.en: If you keep projects small and use flexible media, you don't have to plan as much, and your designs can evolve instead.
sentences.cn: 如果你保持项目小巧并使用灵活的媒介，你就不必做那么多规划，你的设计可以自由进化。

sentences.en: Take as much risk as you can afford.
sentences.cn: 在你能承受的范围内，尽可能多冒险。

sentences.en: In an efficient market, risk is proportionate to reward, so don't look for certainty, but for a bet with high expected value.
sentences.cn: 在一个有效的市场里，风险与回报成正比。别寻求确定性，去寻求那些期望值高（High Expected Value）的赌注。

sentences.en: If you're not failing occasionally, you're probably being too conservative.
sentences.cn: 如果你没有偶尔失败，说明你太保守了。

sentences.en: Though conservatism is usually associated with the old, it's the young who tend to make this mistake.
sentences.cn: 虽然保守通常与老年人联系在一起，但这往往是年轻人的通病。

sentences.en: Inexperience makes them fear risk, but it's when you're young that you can afford the most.
sentences.cn: 经验不足让他们害怕风险，但 年轻正是你最输得起的时候。

sentences.en: Even a project that fails can be valuable.
sentences.cn: 即使失败的项目也是有价值的。

sentences.en: In the process of working on it, you'll have crossed territory few others have seen, and encountered questions few others have asked.
sentences.cn: 在做的过程中，你穿越了无人涉足的领地，遇到了别人未曾问过的问题。

sentences.en: And there's probably no better source of questions than the ones you encounter in trying to do something slightly too hard.
sentences.cn: 没有什么比“试图解决稍稍超出能力范围的问题”更能产生好问题了。

sentences.en: Use the advantages of youth when you have them, and the advantages of age once you have those.
sentences.cn: 年轻时利用年轻的优势，年老时利用年老的优势。

sentences.en: The advantages of youth are energy, time, optimism, and freedom.
sentences.cn: 年轻的优势：精力、时间、乐观、自由。

sentences.en: The advantages of age are knowledge, efficiency, money, and power.
sentences.cn: 年老的优势：知识、效率、金钱、权力。

sentences.en: With effort you can acquire some of the latter when young and keep some of the former when old.
sentences.cn: 努力在年轻时获取一些后者，在年老时保留一些前者。

sentences.en: The old also have the advantage of knowing which advantages they have.
sentences.cn: 年长者还有一个优势：他们清楚自己拥有哪些优势。

sentences.en: The young often have them without realizing it.
sentences.cn: 虽然他们往往不自知。

sentences.en: The biggest is probably time.
sentences.cn: 年轻人最大的优势恐怕是时间，

sentences.en: The young have no idea how rich they are in time.
sentences.cn: 只是他们往往意识不到自己拥有多少时间。

sentences.en: The best way to turn this time to advantage is to use it in slightly frivolous ways: to learn about something you don't need to know about, just out of curiosity, or to try building something just because it would be cool, or to become freakishly good at something.
sentences.cn: 利用时间的最好方式是稍微“挥霍”一下：出于好奇去学点没用的东西，或者纯粹为了耍帅造个东西，或者在某件小事上练到极致。

sentences.en: That "slightly" is an important qualification.
sentences.cn: “稍微”是个重要的限定词。

sentences.en: Spend time lavishly when you're young, but don't simply waste it.
sentences.cn: 年轻时要大方地花时间，但别浪费。

sentences.en: There's a big difference between doing something you worry might be a waste of time and doing something you know for sure will be.
sentences.cn: “担心可能是浪费时间”和“明知是浪费时间”有天壤之别。

sentences.en: The former is at least a bet, and possibly a better one than you think. [ 23 ]
sentences.cn: 前者至少是个赌注，而且往往胜算比你想的大。[23]

sentences.en: The most subtle advantage of youth, or more precisely of inexperience, is that you're seeing everything with fresh eyes.
sentences.cn: 年轻（或者说缺乏经验）最微妙的优势是：你拥有一双新鲜的眼睛。

sentences.en: When your brain embraces an idea for the first time, sometimes the two don't fit together perfectly.
sentences.cn: 当你的大脑第一次接触一个概念时，有时它们并不完全契合。

sentences.en: Usually the problem is with your brain, but occasionally it's with the idea.
sentences.cn: 通常问题出在你的大脑，但偶尔，问题出在概念上。

sentences.en: A piece of it sticks out awkwardly and jabs you when you think about it.
sentences.cn: 某个部分尴尬地凸出来，扎了你一下。

sentences.en: People who are used to the idea have learned to ignore it, but you have the opportunity not to. [ 24 ]
sentences.cn: 习惯了这个概念的人学会了忽略它，但你有机会不忽略。[24]

sentences.en: So when you're learning about something for the first time, pay attention to things that seem wrong or missing.
sentences.cn: 所以，当你初次学习某样东西时，留意那些看起来不对劲或缺失的地方。

sentences.en: You'll be tempted to ignore them, since there's a 99% chance the problem is with you.
sentences.cn: 你会倾向于忽略它们，因为 99% 的概率是你错了。

sentences.en: And you may have to set aside your misgivings temporarily to keep progressing.
sentences.cn: 为了继续学习，你可能得暂时把疑虑搁置。

sentences.en: But don't forget about them.
sentences.cn: 但别忘了它们。

sentences.en: When you've gotten further into the subject, come back and check if they're still there.
sentences.cn: 等你掌握了更多知识，回过头来检查它们是否还在。

sentences.en: If they're still viable in the light of your present knowledge, they probably represent an undiscovered idea.
sentences.cn: 如果还在，那可能就是一个未被发现的想法。

sentences.en: One of the most valuable kinds of knowledge you get from experience is to know what you don't have to worry about.
sentences.cn: 经验带来的最有价值的知识之一，是知道 什么不必担心。

sentences.en: The young know all the things that could matter, but not their relative importance.
sentences.cn: 年轻人知道所有可能重要的事情，但不知道权重的分配。

sentences.en: So they worry equally about everything, when they should worry much more about a few things and hardly at all about the rest.
sentences.cn: 所以他们对所有事都同样担心，而实际上他们应该极度关注少数几件事，忽略其余的。

sentences.en: But what you don't know is only half the problem with inexperience.
sentences.cn: 缺乏经验的另一半问题是：

sentences.en: The other half is what you do know that ain't so.
sentences.cn: 你知道的很多东西并不是真的。

sentences.en: You arrive at adulthood with your head full of nonsense — bad habits you've acquired and false things you've been taught — and you won't be able to do great work till you clear away at least the nonsense in the way of whatever type of work you want to do.
sentences.cn: 成年时，你的脑子里塞满了废话——养成的坏习惯、被灌输的错误观念。在你清除掉那些阻碍你工作的废话之前，你无法成就卓越。

sentences.en: Much of the nonsense left in your head is left there by schools.
sentences.cn: 脑子里的大部分废话是学校留下的。

sentences.en: We're so used to schools that we unconsciously treat going to school as identical with learning, but in fact schools have all sorts of strange qualities that warp our ideas about learning and thinking.
sentences.cn: 我们太习惯于学校，以至于下意识地把“上学”等同于“学习”。但实际上，学校扭曲了我们对学习和思考的认知。例如，

sentences.en: For example, schools induce passivity.
sentences.cn: 学校诱导 被动性。

sentences.en: Since you were a small child, there was an authority at the front of the class telling all of you what you had to learn and then measuring whether you did.
sentences.cn: 从小就有权威告诉你学什么，然后测试你学没学。

sentences.en: But neither classes nor tests are intrinsic to learning; they're just artifacts of the way schools are usually designed.
sentences.cn: 但上课和考试并非学习的本质，它们只是学校设计的产物。

sentences.en: The sooner you overcome this passivity, the better.
sentences.cn: 越早克服这种被动性越好。

sentences.en: If you're still in school, try thinking of your education as your project, and your teachers as working for you rather than vice versa.
sentences.cn: 如果你还在上学，试着把教育看作 你的项目，老师是为你工作的，而不是反过来。

sentences.en: That may seem a stretch, but it's not merely some weird thought experiment.
sentences.cn: 最好的老师不希望做你的老板，他们更希望你冲在前面，

sentences.en: It's the truth economically, and in the best case it's the truth intellectually as well.
sentences.cn: 把他们当作顾问，而不是让他们拖着你走。这听起来可能有些牵强，

sentences.en: The best teachers don't want to be your bosses.
sentences.cn: 但这不仅仅是个古怪的思想实验。

sentences.en: They'd prefer it if you pushed ahead, using them as a source of advice, rather than being pulled by them through the material.
sentences.cn: 从经济角度看这是事实，在最好的情况下，从智识角度看这也是事实。

sentences.en: Schools also give you a misleading impression of what work is like.
sentences.cn: 学校还给你一种关于工作的错误印象：

sentences.en: In school they tell you what the problems are, and they're almost always soluble using no more than you've been taught so far.
sentences.cn: 问题是确定的，且仅靠你所学的知识就总是有解的。而在现实生活中，

sentences.en: In real life you have to figure out what the problems are, and you often don't know if they're soluble at all.
sentences.cn: 你必须自己找出问题是什么，而且往往不知道它是否有解。

sentences.en: But perhaps the worst thing schools do to you is train you to win by hacking the test.
sentences.cn: 最糟糕的是，学校训练你 通过“破解考试”来获胜。

sentences.en: You can't do great work by doing that.
sentences.cn: 你无法通过这种方式成就卓越。

sentences.en: You can't trick God.
sentences.cn: 你骗不了上帝（God / 自然规律）。

sentences.en: So stop looking for that kind of shortcut.
sentences.cn: 别再找捷径了。

sentences.en: The way to beat the system is to focus on problems and solutions that others have overlooked, not to skimp on the work itself.
sentences.cn: 击败系统的办法是专注于别人忽视的问题和解决方案，而不是在工作本身上偷工减料。

sentences.en: Don't think of yourself as dependent on some gatekeeper giving you a "big break." Even if this were true, the best way to get it would be to focus on doing good work rather than chasing influential people.
sentences.cn: 别指望哪个“守门人”给你一个“大机会”。即使这是真的，获得它的最好方式也是专注于做出好作品，而不是追逐权贵。

sentences.en: And don't take rejection by committees to heart.
sentences.cn: 别把委员会的拒绝放在心上。

sentences.en: The qualities that impress admissions officers and prize committees are quite different from those required to do great work.
sentences.cn: 打动招生办或奖项评委的特质，与成就卓越所需的特质截然不同。

sentences.en: The decisions of selection committees are only meaningful to the extent that they're part of a feedback loop, and very few are.
sentences.cn: 选拔委员会的决定只有在作为反馈循环的一部分时才有意义，而这种情况极少见。

sentences.en: People new to a field will often copy existing work.
sentences.cn: 关于模仿：新手模仿现有作品没问题。

sentences.en: There's nothing inherently bad about that.
sentences.cn: 这是学习的最好方式。

sentences.en: There's no better way to learn how something works than by trying to reproduce it.
sentences.cn: 模仿并不一定意味着缺乏原创性。

sentences.en: Nor does copying necessarily make your work unoriginal.
sentences.cn: 原创性是新想法的出现，

sentences.en: Originality is the presence of new ideas, not the absence of old ones.
sentences.cn: 而不是旧想法的缺席。模仿有好坏之分。

sentences.en: There's a good way to copy and a bad way.
sentences.cn: 要模仿，就光明正大地模仿，

sentences.en: If you're going to copy something, do it openly instead of furtively, or worse still, unconsciously.
sentences.cn: 别偷偷摸摸，更别在无意识中模仿。

sentences.en: This is what's meant by the famously misattributed phrase "Great artists steal." The really dangerous kind of copying, the kind that gives copying a bad name, is the kind that's done without realizing it, because you're nothing more than a train running on tracks laid down by someone else.
sentences.cn: 这就是那句被误传的名言“伟大的艺术家偷窃”的真意。真正危险的模仿是无意识的模仿，因为那意味着你只是一列跑在别人铺好的轨道上的火车。但走向另一个极端，

sentences.en: But at the other extreme, copying can be a sign of superiority rather than subordination. [ 25 ]
sentences.cn: 模仿也可能是一种优越而非从属的标志。[25]

sentences.en: In many fields it's almost inevitable that your early work will be in some sense based on other people's.
sentences.cn: 在许多领域，你的早期作品在某种程度上基于他人的作品几乎是不可避免的。

sentences.en: Projects rarely arise in a vacuum.
sentences.cn: 项目很少在真空中产生，

sentences.en: They're usually a reaction to previous work.
sentences.cn: 它们通常是对前人工作的某种回应。

sentences.en: When you're first starting out, you don't have any previous work; if you're going to react to something, it has to be someone else's.
sentences.cn: 当你刚起步时，你没有任何以前的作品；如果你要回应什么，那只能是别人的作品。一旦你立足稳了，

sentences.en: Once you're established, you can react to your own.
sentences.cn: 你就可以回应你自己的作品了。

sentences.en: But while the former gets called derivative and the latter doesn't, structurally the two cases are more similar than they seem.
sentences.cn: 虽然前者被称为“衍生品”而后者不是，但从结构上看，这两种情况比看起来要相似得多。

sentences.en: Oddly enough, the very novelty of the most novel ideas sometimes makes them seem at first to be more derivative than they are.
sentences.cn: 奇怪的是，最新颖的想法，其新颖之处有时反而使它们最初看起来比实际更具衍生性。

sentences.en: New discoveries often have to be conceived initially as variations of existing things, even by their discoverers , because there isn't yet the conceptual vocabulary to express them.
sentences.cn: 新发现往往最初必须被构想为现有事物的变体——甚至对发现者本人也是如此——因为当时还不存在表达它们的全新概念词汇。

sentences.en: There are definitely some dangers to copying, though.
sentences.cn: 不过，模仿确实存在风险。

sentences.en: One is that you'll tend to copy old things — things that were in their day at the frontier of knowledge, but no longer are.
sentences.cn: 一种风险是你会倾向于模仿旧东西——那些在其时代处于知识前沿，但现在已不再前沿的东西。

sentences.en: And when you do copy something, don't copy every feature of it.
sentences.cn: 此外，当你模仿某样东西时，不要模仿它的每一个特征。

sentences.en: Some will make you ridiculous if you do.
sentences.cn: 有些特征如果你照搬，会让你显得很荒谬。

sentences.en: Don't copy the manner of an eminent 50 year old professor if you're 18, for example, or the idiom of a Renaissance poem hundreds of years later.
sentences.cn: 例如，如果你才18岁，不要模仿一位著名的50岁教授的举止；或者在几百年后模仿文艺复兴时期诗歌的措辞。

sentences.en: Some of the features of things you admire are flaws they succeeded despite.
sentences.cn: 你所钦佩的事物中，有些特征其实是瑕疵，

sentences.en: Indeed, the features that are easiest to imitate are the most likely to be the flaws.
sentences.cn: 它是 尽管 有这些瑕疵才成功的。实际上，最容易模仿的特征，往往就是那些瑕疵。

sentences.en: This is particularly true for behavior.
sentences.cn: 在行为举止上尤其如此。

sentences.en: Some talented people are jerks, and this sometimes makes it seem to the inexperienced that being a jerk is part of being talented.
sentences.cn: 有些才华横溢的人是混蛋（Jerks），这有时会让缺乏经验的人误以为“做个混蛋”是“才华横溢”的一部分。并不是；

sentences.en: It isn't; being talented is merely how they get away with it.
sentences.cn: 才华横溢只是他们能以此行事而不被惩罚的资本。

sentences.en: One of the most powerful kinds of copying is to copy something from one field into another.
sentences.cn: 最强有力的模仿之一，是将某个领域的模式复制到另一个领域。

sentences.en: History is so full of chance discoveries of this type that it's probably worth giving chance a hand by deliberately learning about other kinds of work.
sentences.cn: 历史充满了这类偶然发现，所以值得我们可以通过刻意学习其他类型的工作，助“偶然”一臂之力。

sentences.en: You can take ideas from quite distant fields if you let them be metaphors.
sentences.cn: 如果你允许它们成为隐喻，你可以从非常遥远的领域汲取灵感。

sentences.en: Negative examples can be as inspiring as positive ones.
sentences.cn: 反面教材和正面教材一样能给人以此启发。

sentences.en: In fact you can sometimes learn more from things done badly than from things done well; sometimes it only becomes clear what's needed when it's missing.
sentences.cn: 事实上，你有时从做得糟糕的事情中学到的，比从做得好的事情中学到的更多；有时只有当某样东西缺失时，你才清楚什么是必须的。

sentences.en: If a lot of the best people in your field are collected in one place, it's usually a good idea to visit for a while.
sentences.cn: 前往人才聚集地如果你所在领域里许多最优秀的人都聚集在同一个地方，去那里待一阵子通常是个好主意。
